summary: David A. Hall is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shoshin Ichishima in 1976 and earned a doctorate from the University of California, Berkeley in 1990. He was a visiting scholar at Taisho University in 1977.
David Azzopardi is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Kate Crosby (attested 2010).

David B. Gray specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Ryuichi Abe. His appointments include a postdoctoral fellowship at Rice University and teaching at Santa Clara University.

David Brainerd Spooner (1879–1925) was an Indologist and archaeologist. After studying at Stanford University from around 1895 to 1899, he served with the Archaeological Survey of India from circa 1906 until 1925 as Directeur p. i.
David Brick is an Indology scholar who studied under Patrick Olivelle (attested 2009). He served as a professor at Yale University, attested between 2012 and 2018.

David Brown (1762–1812) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied as a sizar at Magdalene College, Cambridge in 1782 and served as Provost at Fort William College from circa 1800 to 1807.

David Bubna-Litic works in Buddhist studies and related fields. He earned his PhD at Western Sydney University and served as a Lecturer in Strategic Management and Responsible Business at the University of Technology Sydney, attested in 2000.

David Burton is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Bristol (1994–1997). He held posts at Keble College, Oxford (attested 2001) and Canterbury Christ Church University (attested 2010).

David Dean Shulman is an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. under John Ralston Marr at SOAS, University of London (1972–1976). He held multiple positions at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, including Professor of Indian Studies and Comparative Religion from 1985.

David Drewes is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia in 2006 under Karen Christina Lang and served as an Assistant Professor of Religion at the University of Manitoba (attested 2008–2010).

David E. Cooper is a philosopher who studied at St Edmund Hall from around 1961 to 1965. He lectured at the University of Oxford in 1967 and served as Professor of Philosophy at Durham University from 1986 to 2008.

David E. Riggs is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from UCLA. He taught at UC Santa Barbara, UIUC, and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and was a researcher at Nichibunken (attested 2006).

David Faure is a historian and sinologist who earned a sociology PhD at Princeton (~1970–1976). He lectured in Modern Chinese History at St Antony's College from 1990 and served as director at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~2006).

David Fiordalis specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez and served as associate professor and chair of religious studies at Linfield University (attested 2017).

David Friedman (1903–1984) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies philosopher. He served as Reader in Indian Philosophy at SOAS, University of London (~1950–1970) and was attested as Professor at the University of London in 1969.

David Gellner is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He has held positions at the University of Oxford, including Emeritus Professor of Social Anthropology at Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2026).

David Germano is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992. He has served as a faculty member and Associate Professor at the University of Virginia.
David Gonsalez is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. His training includes traditional study under Lobsang Choephel, Lati Rinpoche, Kirti Tsenshab Rinpoche, and Denma Lochö Rinpoche.

David Gordon White is an Indologist and historian of religion who earned his doctorate from the University of Chicago (~1979–1988). He taught at the University of Virginia before serving as professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara from 1996.

David Higgins is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He has held research positions at the University of Vienna (attested 2015) and as a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
